context_ladder.adjudicated_provenance: Read in full context by Claude (claude-sonnet-5-5) on 2026-09-30, then corrected by the maintainer's rulings the same day; NOT otherwise reviewed by the maintainer. Sample: the 7 real items on which the three tiers disagreed (i8, i15, i16, i18, i19, i25, i28) plus 8 of the 27 items on which all tiers agreed, drawn at random with seed 3 (i12, i20, i27, i6 yes; i22, i29, i2, i0 no). Null means Uncertain and is excluded from accuracy: i15 (a stormwater drainage concern at a rezoning hearing; maintainer: marginal, does not reach the policy of stormwater, not an automatic yes) and i25 (a named zoning case continued on a procedural item; by the maintainer's rubric this may be a yes, pending confirmation). i18 was changed to yes: the consent agenda includes a specific drainage project (Glasgow and Paisley drainage improvements) although the matched phrase sits in a generic services contract. The disagreement items are the hard ones, so accuracy on this subset is a lower bound, not an estimate of general accuracy. Replace or extend with audit-verified labels as they exist.
context_ladder.rubric: Maintainer policy 2026-09-30: a tag is correct when the chapter involves a SPECIFIC project, contract, program or policy on the topic, even when it is approved routinely (for example on a consent agenda); it is not correct for a generic mention, a passing reference in a list or summary, a read-back of past items, or a general-purpose services contract not tied to a specific project or policy on the topic. Project exposure, not only contested debate, is what the tags are for.

notes: Controls are real excerpts paired with a tag from an unrelated taxonomy group; they must be rejected. No ground truth exists for pull-quote quality; that experiment measures consistency only.
